newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut market ends week dragged down by Solidere.
newsitem.headline: Beirut market ends week dragged down by Solidere.

text.p: The Beirut Stock Exchange ended the week on a low note on Thursday and brokers said sliding Solidere shares pulled the market down.
"Solidere set the pace in the market which ended the week on a low note," Georges Abou Jaoude, director of Lebanese operations at Financial Funds Advisors, said.
Solidere A shares fell 9.5 percent in the week to $10.5 from $11.5 while B shares fell 7.7 percent to $11.375 from $12.25.

Two of three listed banks also fell. Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce fell for the first time since its listing on December 20 to $16.25 from $17.25. Banque Audi traded at $20 from $20.125 while Bank of Beirut held steady at $3.5625.
"There is an opportunity cost in investing in Solidere -- staying at low levels while you can go for fast cash elsewhere," Abou Jaoude said.
"Lebanon is not a long-term investment market yet. Solidere shares have a very good value but everyone is waiting for the day when the distribution of A shares ends," he added.
The A and B shares hit 16-month highs of $11.75 and $12.25 last week after the company's GDRs soared in London on reports of buying by U.S. and European emerging market funds.

"The problem with Solidere shares is the continuous heavy supply of A shares placed by former property rights holders who are eager to realise their cash," broker Carole Deeb of Credit Commercial et Foncier said.
"I expect B shares to pick up a bit next week," she added.
The LISPI general index fell two percent on the week to 86.54 and the BLOM general index fell 6.71 percent to 930.32. The LIBX bank index fell 2.17 percent to 136.71.
Audi and BOB traded in heavy demand throughout the week. Demand on BLC picked up on Thursday two days after the bank announced "very good" quarterly profits.
"BLC fell in profit-taking. Demand is coming back after the very good quarterly results and after profit-taking investors got out and bargain hunters started to come in," Abou Jaoude said.
"As for BOB, I think demand will come back by mid-June after the bank announces results for its second quarter, which we think will be very positive," he added.
On Tuesday, BLC announced a $5.2 million pre-tax profit for the first three months of the year and dealers said the results were in line with the bank's forecasts and market expectations.
Last month, BOB reported a 29.61 percent rise in net profits over the same period.
"I think we will witness a short period of stability for bank shares in the near future," Deeb said.
Of the four listed industrial shares, Ciments Libanais traded unchanged at $1.2812 and Eternit held steady at $1.875. Both shares traded only on Monday.
There was no trade in either Ciments Blancs and tilemaker Uniceramic.
Total BSE turnover for the week shortened to four days by Friday's public holiday was 761,420 for a value of $7,275,535 from last week's 970,240 shares for a value of $9,687,292.
- Zeina Soufan, Beirut editoria (9611) 745307 745308
